children: Arabica coffee futures on ICE rose on Monday, after hitting a fresh 10-week low earlier, on looming increases in certified stocks and rains in top grower Brazil.
Cocoa and sugar steadied meanwhile.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
rose 0.8% to $2.8795 per lb at 1440 GMT, having set a fresh 10-week low of $2.8150.
* Exchange data showed nearly 65,000 bags of arabica (KC-TOT-PENDING) are pending grading or quality controls so they can be certified as deliverable against ICE contracts.

* Dealers, brokers and analysts told Reuters last week that traders are planning, over the next couple of months, to deliver at least 300,000 bags of arabica to ICE exchange warehouses, where stocks have sunk to 26-year lows.
* A broker said the potential for rising stocks plus flowering in Brazil thanks to the rains is putting arabica under pressure overall.
* Robusta coffee
fell 0.2% to $3,516 a ton.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
was little changed at 18.14 cents per lb, having hit a 16-month peak of 18.88 last week.
* The U.S. Department of Agriculture has cut its 2026/27 sugar production forecast to 8.84 million short tons (ST), the smallest volume since 2019/20.

* Sugar also remains underpinned by looming supply tightness in India, Thailand and Europe, as well as strength in energy markets, which can encourage more use of cane to make the biofuel ethanol rather than sugar.
* Oil prices rose on Monday, remaining above $100 a barrel as the U.S.-Iran war put more Gulf oil supplies out of reach.
* White sugar
rose 0.4% to $525.10 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​​rose 0.6% to £4,357 per ton, having lost 4% last week.

* From the start of the 2026/27 season on September 1 to September 13, cocoa arrivals at ports in top grower Ivory Coast reached 26,000 tons, down 45.8% from the same period in the previous season, which began on October 1.
* Below-average rainfall last week in most of Ivory Coast's main cocoa-growing regions could cause the September-to-February main crop to end earlier than last season, farmers said.

* "Two risks sit outside the current (cocoa) price. EUDR compliance (struggles) and stronger Harmattan (winds). For now the market is willing to look past it and trade decent short-term availability," said commodity intelligence firm Vesper.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.4% to $5,982 a ton.
